name: Monotonic Renumeration
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ integers. Let's denote monotonic renumeration of array $$$a$$$ as an array $$$b$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ integers such that all of the following conditions are met: $$$b_1 = 0$$$; for every pair of indices $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ such that $$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$, if $$$a_i = a_j$$$, then $$$b_i = b_j$$$ (note that if $$$a_i \ne a_j$$$, it is still possible that $$$b_i = b_j$$$); for every index $$$i \in [1, n - 1]$$$ either $$$b_i = b_{i + 1}$$$ or $$$b_i + 1 = b_{i + 1}$$$. For example, if $$$a = [1, 2, 1, 2, 3]$$$, then two possible monotonic renumerations of $$$a$$$ are $$$b = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]$$$ and $$$b = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1]$$$. Your task is to calculate the number of different monotonic renumerations of $$$a$$$. The answer may be large, so print it modulo $$$998244353$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of elements in $$$a$$$. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$).
output_specification: Print one integer — the number of different monotonic renumerations of $$$a$$$, taken modulo $$$998244353$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to N using Fermat's Little Theorem (mod 10^9+7 or 998244353). Answer nCr queries in O(1) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1102E — Monotonic Renumeration [310. Large Factorials and Binomial Coefficients]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Combinatorial selection $\binom{N}{K} = \frac{N!}{K!(N-K)!} \pmod P$ can be evaluated in $O(1)$ by precomputing factorials $fact[i] = fact[i-1] \cdot i \pmod P$ and inverse factorials $invFact[i] = invFact[i+1] \cdot (i+1) \pmod P$ using Fermat's Little Theorem $a^{P-2} \equiv a^{-1} \pmod P$.
